one_line.text: An American self-help author, podcaster, and speaker known for turning behaviour-change ideas into simple verbal tools.

biography.text: Robbins trained and worked as a lawyer before moving through media commentary, speaking, books, and podcasting. Her 2011 TEDx talk and later book The 5 Second Rule established her practical, high-energy approach; she now hosts The Mel Robbins Podcast and runs the media company 143 Studios.

background.text: She earned a law degree from Boston College, worked in legal aid and as a public defender, then built a career in television commentary, coaching-style speaking, publishing, and independently produced audio and video.

expertise.text: Her demonstrated expertise is communicating practical behaviour-change and motivation frameworks to a broad audience, supported by long experience interviewing specialists and producing self-improvement media. She is not presented by the independent profiles as a psychologist, psychiatrist, or academic researcher.

perspective_and_limits.text: Robbins writes as a practitioner and mass-market communicator. Her strength is making an action memorable enough to use under stress; readers should distinguish that communication skill from clinical authority and check broad psychological or neurological claims against specialist evidence.
